text: A commit stores the full set of tracked files as they stood at that moment, together with an author, a time, a message and a link to the commit before it, rather than a line-by-line diff.
A branch is a movable label that points at one commit, and HEAD is the pointer that says which commit, and usually which branch, you are currently on.
Staging changes on purpose, rather than adding everything out of habit, lets you check the staged content with a diff command before committing it.
A merge commit can record two parent commits at once.
